project.name: Design Chamber
project.pitch: an OpenChamber desktop-app extension that renders Claude-Design-style design canvases and full-screen HTML pages inside OpenChamber, from plain files the user's own chat agent writes to `~/Documents/Designs`
project.stack: TypeScript strict, OpenChamber SDK apiVersion 1, a sandboxed-iframe rail panel and full-screen page bundled as IIFE with esbuild, a local Node service process, `node:test`
personas: **The OpenChamber user** (designer-developer who chats with an agent to produce designs and wants to see, comment on, version and export them without leaving OpenChamber)
**The chat agent** (the user's own agent in OpenChamber, the author of every design file)

pages.name: Rail panel
pages.one_liner: The navigator in OpenChamber's rail: browse designs, compact viewer, settings.

pages.name: Full-screen page
pages.one_liner: The library, the canvas wall and the page viewer.

pages.name: Library: projects and folders
pages.one_liner: The page's designs list grouped by project and by the user's folders.

pages.name: Rail: projects and folders
pages.one_liner: The rail's Show select, Filters area, systems entry and folder actions.

pages.name: Design systems
pages.one_liner: The list of design systems and the New design system sheet.

pages.name: Viewer: a design's system
pages.one_liner: The system chip, popover, update banner and sheet.

pages.name: Settings: Design systems
pages.one_liner: The default and per-project pins, and the New design dialog's system field.

project.roles: the OpenChamber user, the chat agent that writes the files, and an untrusted design running in its sandboxed iframe (including a first run with no designs folder and a changed designs folder)
project.core_flows: browse the designs list → open a page and export ZIP/HTML · open a design canvas wall → pan/zoom · add a comment pin → send it to chat · restore a version · change the designs folder

`node --test --test-concurrency=1 "test/**/*.test.ts"` (Node ≥ 22.18 strips the types; one file: `node --test test/shared/design-json.test.ts`).
the SDK's own package checker on the built manifest, HTML entries and service (run `npm run build` first); CI runs it after `npm run check`.
release zip `design-chamber-<version>.zip` (run `npm run build` first; publishing it is user-gated).

the visual harness, after `npm run build`: the built UI behind a mock host and the in-memory fake service, in headless Chrome, rail at 320 and 480 px and the page at 1400 px, dark and light; every `test/ui/visual/scenarios/*.mjs` runs, `<filter>` is a regex on the name. Not part of `npm test`. Always pass `--out`: the default writes into the tracked `documentation/pages/img/`. Chrome not at the usual path → set `DC_TEST_CHROME`.

re-render the agent team from `.agents/team.json` (the skill renderer, then the project fixes for em dashes and generic database wording), then run `node .agents/verify-team.cjs`. After a render, only the `team:start` to `team:end` block of this file is regenerated; the rest is edited by hand.

commands.gates_note: all three pass before any task is done; `npm run check` runs them together. No dev or watch command: there is no dev server by design (`docs/SPEC.md` §1); rebuild with `npm run build`.

stack.hygiene_rule: `strict: true`; zero `any`; no non-null `!` without a comment
stack.hygiene_check: zero `any`; no non-null `!` without a comment; no `console.log` shipped
stack.env_convention: the service bearer token is generated per run and never written to a bundle, a log or `design.json`; a `.env`, if ever used, is git-ignored with `.env.example` committed
stack.unsafe_render_apis: `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write`, `eval`, `new Function`, an iframe `sandbox` that combines `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` for untrusted content, a `postMessage` with a `'*'` target for privileged messages
stack.secret_files: `.env` (if one is ever created; none is expected)
stack.secret_locations: the running service's memory: the bearer token is generated per service run, held only by the service and the host-side caller, and never reaches a bundle, a log line, `design.json`, a report or a guest iframe
stack.breakpoints: the rail-panel width (320 and 480 px) and the full-screen page, in light and dark
stack.boundaries: loopback service requests, `design.json` and other files read from disk (agent-written, untrusted), the guest-iframe postMessage channel, host SDK messages, persisted settings
stack.discipline_rule: OpenChamber SDK `apiVersion: 1` only, with APIs as documented in `~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber/packages/sdk/` (`DOCUMENTATION.md`, `API.md`, `GUEST_SERVICES.md`, `examples/`; read-only reference). The manifest never declares `provides: ["browser"]` (it would fight Design Canvas). Guests are IIFE bundles built by esbuild; no dev server and no external-Chrome-window architecture (that is `openchamber-design-canvas`, a reference for reusable pieces only). The architecture and lanes authority is `docs/SPEC.md`.
stack.discipline_line: OpenChamber SDK `apiVersion: 1` APIs only; no `provides: ["browser"]`; guests are IIFE bundles; `docs/SPEC.md` consulted for architecture and lanes
stack.stack_checks: SDK `apiVersion: 1` only; no `provides: ["browser"]`; guests are esbuild IIFE bundles; tests use `node:test`; `tsc --strict` clean; `npm run guest-check` clean for a manifest or entry change; layout matches `docs/SPEC.md` §12 (code wins, flag drift); no em dash in any string under `src/` (`test/copy-no-em-dash.test.ts`)
stack.stack_violation: a dev-server or external-Chrome-window dependency, a hard-coded colour that ignores the host theme
stack.styling_rule: Theme fidelity: colours, type and radii come from the host theme tokens (`ready.theme.tokens`, applied as `--oc-*` CSS variables) and the `@openchamber/sdk/ui` kit (`--oc-sdk-*`, `.oc-sdk-*`), spacing from `--dc-s1` to `--dc-s6` in `src/ui/styles.css`, never hard-coded; the UI follows a theme switch live (light and dark both checked). Nothing global leaks into a design and nothing from a design leaks into the host.
stack.client_rule: Reach the host only through `@openchamber/sdk` (read-only reference: `~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber/packages/sdk/`); never hand-roll host messaging; never edit the OpenChamber source. The loopback service binds to 127.0.0.1 only; every route verifies the bearer token before acting (`src/service/http.ts`); every path is resolved inside the designs root through `resolveInside` in `src/service/paths.ts` (rejecting `..`, absolute paths, encoded and backslash variants, drive-letter tricks, symlink escapes) before any read or write. A new route without a rejecting test for a missing or wrong token and for a traversal attempt is not done.
stack.server_unit_names: service routes in `src/service/routes/*.ts`, called by the panel and page through `src/guest/service-client.ts`; guest iframes (untrusted design HTML) never receive the token, the host bridge or any route
stack.access_control_rule: Every design states: for every new service route, the bearer-token check and the path-containment step; for every new iframe surface, its `sandbox` flags, CSP and feed (srcdoc/blob); input validation points (requests, `design.json`, agent-written files); what crosses the postMessage boundary; secrets handling (the token never reaches a bundle, a log, a file or a guest). Every new UI surface names the host theme tokens it uses.
stack.access_control_check: Every new route has its token check and containment designed · every untrusted-HTML surface names sandbox flags and CSP · colours come from host theme tokens
stack.schema_units: route, shared type, `design.json` field, component, hook and state
stack.schema_locations: `docs/SPEC.md`, the shared types under `src/shared/**`, and the SDK docs in `~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber/packages/sdk/`
stack.impl_order: shared types → path containment and auth → service routes → host bridge → guest logic; the presentation in `src/ui/**` is ui-ux-developer's
stack.ui_impl_order: component → panel/page wiring → states → theme (light and dark) check
stack.flow_shape: agent writes files → service (watch, validate, serve) → host bridge → guest iframe → comment or revision back to the linked chat
stack.data_change_shape: files and `design.json` fields under `Designs/<slug>/`, settings keys, cache layout (thumbnails), snapshot format in `.versions/`, and backward-readability for existing designs
stack.error_shape: an `ApiErrorBody` `{ error, message }` from `src/shared/api.ts` with its status from `API_ERROR_STATUS`, `message` being the plain sentence the panel shows
stack.data_principles: Files on disk are the source of truth, one folder per item; the service holds no state beyond caches; writes are atomic (temp + rename) and snapshot first; existing designs are never moved silently.
stack.stack_edge_cases: partial writes by the agent while the watcher fires, a missing or changed designs folder, a theme switch mid-render, a malformed or huge `design.json`, headless Chrome missing (thumbnail fallback), service restart, Windows path quirks (backslashes, drive letters, case-insensitive filesystem)
stack.early_items_step: Confirm the types and props the service and host bridge expose (`src/shared/**`) so nothing downstream blocks; flag a missing field instead of inventing one.
stack.data_layer_summary: all non-presentation code: the local Node service (`src/service/**`: routes, bearer auth, path containment, file watching, versions, thumbnails, checks, ZIP and single-file export), shared types and the `design.json` contract (`src/shared/**`), the SDK host bridge and non-visual guest logic (`src/guest/**`: service client, store, camera pan/zoom math, frame-doc, anchoring, comments, versions, flows), the `dc` check CLI (`src/cli/**`), the OpenCode plugin (`src/plugin/**`), and `test/**` except `test/ui/**`
stack.ui_territory_summary: `src/ui/**` and `test/ui/**`: panel and page markup, styles, the rail, the page, the wall, the Work Status and chat-block frames, the design-system screens, components, pure view models, the viewer chrome around the design iframes, view-model tests and the visual harness

migration.rule: `design.json` is a contract. Its shape comes from `docs/SPEC.md` §6 and `docs/BRIEF.md`; a change to it is versioned, still reads existing designs (an old `"artifact"` reads as a page), and starts as the architect's spec, not as a code edit. The WP0 interface files (`src/shared/{types,api,limits,bridge-protocol,design-json}.ts`, `src/service/{main,http,context}.ts`) change only through the main agent.
migration.state_step: Read the part of `docs/SPEC.md` this task touches (lane in §12, contract in §6, routes in §7); if it disagrees with the code, report the discrepancy before building.

money.rule: Filesystem writes are contained and reversible. Every write goes through the single path-containment module (`src/service/paths.ts`); nothing is written outside the designs root; nothing the service did not create is overwritten or deleted; a version snapshot precedes a destructive change; changing the designs folder never moves existing designs silently. After touching any of it, run `npm test` and quote the output.

stack.security_examples: a token-less or path-escaping service route, an iframe `sandbox` loosened or its CSP dropped, the bearer token in a bundle, a log or a guest, agent HTML injected into the host DOM

risk.surfaces: the guest-iframe sandbox/CSP boundary, loopback service security (bearer auth and path containment under the designs root), filesystem writes under the user's Documents, rendering untrusted agent-written HTML, theme fidelity with OpenChamber
risk.paths: the service's auth and path-containment code (`src/service/http.ts`, `src/service/paths.ts`, `src/shared/path-compare.ts`), the iframe `sandbox`/CSP attributes and the srcdoc/blob feed (`src/guest/frame-doc.ts`, `src/guest/frame-channel.ts`, `src/guest/bridge/**`), and every filesystem write under the designs root (paths per `docs/SPEC.md`)
risk.critical: a write outside the designs root, an overwritten or deleted user file, a silently moved design, a non-v1 SDK API or `provides: ["browser"]` declared
risk.escalation: service auth, path containment, the iframe sandbox/CSP, the guest bridge or filesystem writes
risk.rule: Untrusted HTML is rendered only inside a sandboxed iframe, and path resolution is one pure, tested function (`resolveInside` in `src/service/paths.ts`). Every design that touches either names the sandbox flags, the CSP, the feed, the messages that cross the boundary, and which function resolves paths under the designs root and what its tests must cover.
risk.section: Sandbox & Path Safety (sandbox flags, CSP, the containment function and the tests it needs)
risk.check: Untrusted-content iframes carry no `allow-same-origin`; every service route checks the bearer token and resolves paths inside the designs root; colours come from host theme tokens
qa_sections: **Sandbox & CSP**: every guest iframe has `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin` for agent HTML, a CSP, a srcdoc/blob feed, and `postMessage` source/origin checked both ways; the token and host bridge never reach a guest. Try a design that attempts to read `parent`, call the service, and navigate the top frame.

**Loopback service**: bound to 127.0.0.1; bearer token required on every route, assets, thumbnails and export included; wrong and missing token rejected; path containment attacked with `..`, absolute paths, encoded and backslash variants, drive letters and symlinks.

**Filesystem writes**: only inside the designs root; atomic; snapshot before overwrite; nothing deleted that the service did not create (Delete moves a design to `<root>/.trash`); changing the folder never moves existing designs; behaviour on a missing or unwritable folder.

**Untrusted HTML**: renders only in a sandboxed iframe; single-file export inlines assets without executing anything; comment selectors and snippets are escaped wherever shown or sent to chat; thumbnails fall back to a live mini-iframe when headless Chrome is missing.
**Theme fidelity**: host tokens only (grep UI sources for raw hex), live theme switch, light and dark, contrast at AA.

gated.deploy_commands: publishing or releasing the extension (`npm publish`, tags, GitHub releases), `gh repo create`, `gh pr create` / `gh pr merge`, uninstalling or deleting any OpenChamber extension the agent did not install itself, deleting anything under `~/Documents/Designs` the agent did not create, `rm -rf` outside this repo, any edit to the OpenChamber source (`~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber`) or `~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber-design-canvas` (both read-only references)
gated.live_tools: GitHub via `gh`, the user's running OpenChamber beyond a folder-install smoke test, a chat turn started from a test (a paid model call)

design.direction: native fidelity. The extension must look like part of OpenChamber in the rail panel (320 to 480 px) and the full-screen page: host theme tokens and the `@openchamber/sdk/ui` kit, no palette or typeface of our own. Colours follow the active OpenChamber theme live.
design.token_source: the OpenChamber host theme tokens (`ready.theme.tokens`, applied as `--oc-*` CSS variables) and the `@openchamber/sdk/ui` kit look (`--oc-sdk-*`), spacing from `--dc-s1` to `--dc-s6` in `src/ui/styles.css`; never a raw hex or a one-off size (a design's own `tokens.css` is design content for the guest, not host chrome)
conventions: Core flows (each has a step budget): browse the designs list → open a page and export ZIP/HTML · open a design canvas wall → pan/zoom · add a comment pin → send it to chat · restore a version · change the designs folder

- Glossary (one term per concept): **design** = an item folder; **page** = a single HTML page design shown full screen (formerly "artifact"); **canvas** = a multi-screen design wall; **screen** = one page of a canvas; **viewport** = a device size; **artboard** = a screen at a viewport; **pin** = an element-anchored comment; **version** = a snapshot
- Copy: plain words, no em dash in any text a user or an agent reads (`test/copy-no-em-dash.test.ts` scans every string under `src/`)
- Controls from the `@openchamber/sdk/ui` kit; breakpoints are n/a in the web sense

gotchas: - **Sources of truth:** `docs/BRIEF.md` (owner decisions; anything not listed there is open, so ask, don't guess; edit it only on the user's instruction) and `docs/SPEC.md` (the technical spec, the authority for architecture and lanes; changes go through the architect).

- **OpenChamber SDK `apiVersion: 1`, target OpenChamber >= 2.7.0 (SDK 2.7.0, pinned in `package.json`).** Reference docs live in `~/Documents/GitHub/openchamber/packages/sdk/` (`DOCUMENTATION.md`, `API.md`, `GUEST_SERVICES.md`, `examples/`), read-only; verify an API there before using it.
- **Never declare `provides: ["browser"]`.** It would fight Design Canvas.

- **`openchamber-design-canvas` (v0.3.0, MIT, same owner) is a parts bin, not a base.** Reuse Chrome discovery, wall pan/zoom math, design-system precedence, prompt rules, presets and gates; do not inherit its external-Chrome-window + Vite-dev-server architecture. Read-only. Design Chamber is not that tool: rendering is in-app.

- **Agent-written HTML is untrusted.** It renders only in a sandboxed srcdoc/blob iframe with a CSP; never combine `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin`; `postMessage` source and origin are checked both ways; guests never see the bearer token or host bridge; agent HTML never goes into the host DOM.

- **The designs root is user data.** Default `~/Documents/Designs`, changeable (persisted setting); existing designs are never silently moved; every path is resolved and contained under the root before use. Tests and browser checks always run on a scratch root (`test/helpers/tmp-root.ts`, `DC_SETTINGS_PATH`, or a scratch folder applied in Settings and switched back afterwards), never on the real one.

- **Windows host.** Backslashes, drive letters and a case-insensitive filesystem make naive `startsWith` containment checks unsafe; use the one tested containment function (`resolveInside` in `src/service/paths.ts`, comparisons in `src/shared/path-compare.ts`).
- **Guests are IIFE bundles** (esbuild): no runtime ESM imports, no dev server.

- **No dev server, so a UI change is seen in the visual harness or a folder install.** The harness (`test/ui/visual/shoot.mjs`, Dev commands) runs the built UI on a fake service; folder-installing this extension into the user's running OpenChamber for smoke tests is allowed (`docs/BRIEF.md`; steps in `documentation/smoke/REPORT.md` and the browser-tester file).
- **`rules/**` (design-rules content: bundled presets and agent instructions) is written by a separate rules author**, not by this roster: read it, don't edit it unless the task is about it.

- **The WP0 interface files change only through the main agent**, who notifies every lane (`docs/SPEC.md` §14): `src/shared/{types,api,limits,bridge-protocol,design-json}.ts` and `src/service/{main,http,context}.ts`. Files two builders both touch (the panel/page entry `src/ui/main.ts`, shared types the UI imports) are sequenced by the main agent. The layout is `docs/SPEC.md` §12; if it and this file disagree, the spec wins.

- **Process:** GitHub repo `design-chamber` (public, MIT), default branch `master`, protected: no direct pushes. Work on a branch, open a PR (template in `.github/`); CI (Ubuntu, Windows, Fedora; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass and 1 approval is required; only the owner merges (bypass). Head branches auto-delete. macOS is not in CI: run `npm run check` on a Mac for macOS-affecting changes. Pushing a branch and opening a PR are still user-gated (protocol §6).
- **`.env` is not expected.** If one is ever created it may be read and updated; its values never reach a commit, a log or a report.
architecture: Authority: `docs/SPEC.md` (changes go through the architect); this section is a summary.

- Rail `panel` = navigator; full-screen `page` = viewer/canvas; both sandboxed-iframe guests of the OpenChamber extension host, fed by the extension's local Node `service` (loopback, bearer-authenticated).

- Storage: one folder per item, `Designs/<slug>/` with `design.json` (`kind: "page" | "canvas"`; old `"artifact"` reads as a page; title, created/updated, linked `sessionId`, viewports, screens, comments), `index.html` (page) or `screens/*.html` (canvas), `assets/`, `DESIGN.md` + `tokens.css`, `.versions/`.

- Design systems (Phase 2.5): a system lives in `Designs/_systems/<id>/` (internal) or in the project repo with a generated living page (repo-backed, the repo is the source of truth). Each design keeps its own copy in `<design>/system/` (copy-on-link) with overrides and "Reset to system". The service never writes a project repo; only the agent does, after the user approves a reviewed diff in the system's chat. `/design-system` + the `design-system-builder` skill build a system; designs group by project and manual folders (`docs/SPEC.md` §6.7 to §6.9).

- The chat agent writes the files; the service watches the folder and the UI refreshes live. `/design <brief>` (canvas) and `/page <brief>` attach the design rules, target folder and `design.json` contract to any chat.

- Agents without the slash command find Design Chamber through `<root>/AGENTS.md` (a guide the service keeps current, never over a user-edited file) and an optional `design-chamber` skill installed from Settings (spec: `documentation/specs/agent-guidance-and-pages.md`).
- Thumbnails: headless-Chrome PNGs cached on change; fallback to a live mini-iframe when Chrome is missing.

- Checks: the agent runs `dc check <slug>` through a launcher the service writes in `<root>/.chamber/bin/` (no token; renders every artboard offline in headless Chrome over a pipe, writes `.chamber/check.json` and PNGs); the viewer shows a Checks badge with "Ask the agent to fix" (`docs/SPEC.md` §9.9).

- Review loop: a build strip shows what the linked agent is doing, an ask bar under the wall sends the user's words (optionally about one element) to the linked chat, pins can be sent one at a time, and a restore offers Undo instead of a confirm (`docs/SPEC.md` §13.3).
business_rules: Product decisions are in `docs/BRIEF.md`; anything not listed there is open: ask, never guess.

| Design-rules precedence (highest first) | 1 the user's words in chat · 2 the active project's design rules (DESIGN.md, token/theme files, AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md design sections, existing breakpoints) · 3 chosen bundled style preset · 4 per-design `DESIGN.md` + `tokens.css` once confirmed · 5 built-in anti-slop rules |
| Default viewports | Laptop 1280×800, Phone 390×844; derive from the project first; ask when unsure |
| Page export | ZIP (html + assets) and single-file HTML (assets inlined) |

| Design canvas | infinite wall, pan/zoom, multiple screens × viewports as artboards; Edit/Play modes; element-anchored comment pins (selector/snippet travels with the comment); "send comments" = one revision request to the linked chat; version snapshot per agent turn, compare/restore |
| Linked chat | each design remembers its `sessionId`; "Continue in chat" reopens it; new chat if none/gone |
data_rules: - Loopback-only (127.0.0.1), bearer-authenticated; the host passes the port and token in `OPENCHAMBER_SERVICE_PORT` / `OPENCHAMBER_SERVICE_TOKEN`; routes are `docs/SPEC.md` §7, typed in `src/shared/api.ts`.
- Every path is contained under the designs root (`resolveInside` in `src/service/paths.ts`) before any read or write; every route checks the bearer token (`src/service/http.ts`).
- Mutations (writes, restores, exports, settings) are service routes called by the panel and page; guest iframes never get the token or a route.

- `DC_SETTINGS_PATH` points the service at another settings file (a test seam; the host never passes it), which is how a test or a local check gets its own designs root (`test/helpers/service-process.ts`).
- Deploy-type commands (publish, release, `gh repo create`, PRs, push) wait for the user's go-ahead.

ui-ux-developer.description: Use when building or modifying UI components, pages, styling, layouts, or any visual or accessibility work, to a designed, non-generic standard. The data layer ({{stack.data_layer_summary}}) belongs to backend-developer.

qa-tester.focus: Verification after M/L tasks, risk-surface changes and user-visible features; regression tests (`test/**`); 🟣 entries in `documentation/known-issues.md`; never fixes production code
qa-tester.escalate: the strongest model available for a high-stakes change on a risk surface, or a task that has already failed QA once
qa-tester.work_type: Verification, review of a finished task
qa-tester.description: Use when reviewing code for correctness, verifying bug fixes, running quality gates, or auditing a feature for security, edge cases and quality issues. Use PROACTIVELY after any M or L implementation task, any task on a risk surface, and any user-visible feature. Reports findings, never fixes production code.

browser-tester.escalate: up to opus when a flow fails in a way you cannot pin to a step
browser-tester.work_type: Browser testing, the second QA step for UI changes
browser-tester.description: Use after qa-tester passes a change the user will see, as the second QA step. Walks the changed flow in the visual harness or a folder-installed OpenChamber on a scratch designs root, at the rail width and on the full-screen page, dark and light, and reports what broke with screenshots. Never touches the real ~/Documents/Designs, never reads the diff for bugs, never fixes code.
browser-tester.focus: Second QA step for changes the user sees: walks the changed flow in the visual harness or a folder-installed OpenChamber, always on a scratch designs root, rail 320 and 480 px and the full-screen page, dark and light, with screenshots

code-reviewer.focus: Independent review of a diff, on the user's request; logs minor issues to `documentation/known-issues.md`

post_render._note: Applied by .agents/render.js after the skill renders. Each exact `from` must match at least once or the render stops, so a template change is noticed. Then every em dash left in a generated file is replaced.
